scope: Real authored mouse strokes, production crop/segmentation/symbol repair/chunking/fallback/cache, real FP32 model, real KaTeX preview, native answer transport and public native grading APIs. No expected equation is injected into OCR.
limitations: Fixed authored stroke probes; no pupil data. These counts measure this sample, not general handwriting accuracy or statistical confidence.
One repeat per case and snapshot. Load, first inference, recognition and cache resubmission are separate measurements; no general speedup claim.
The task holdout was previously evaluated and is not untouched after these fixes.
Two ambiguous controls have identical authored pixels but different intended case; their results are separate from the ten explicit probes.
Old eleven probes are unassessed for letter distinction, correcting the initial source default label without changing its raw report.
accepted=false/outcome=unknown is unresolved, not a proved correct rejection. acceptedFlagAgreement and conclusiveGradeAgreement are separate.
A matching grade does not establish OCR fidelity. case-wrong-xX-step is already refused for its OCR-mismatching given system; this does not locate the intended erroneous middle step.
DPR2 is diagnostic only, with saveImages=true in TEMP. Its times are not directly compared with DPR1 saveImages=false. No strokes, events, freeze data or images are embedded.

Model-call wall durations include overlapping queue waits; their sum is neither pipeline elapsed time nor isolated inference time. Case timings are rounded to 0.001 ms; transcription metrics and source hashes are preserved.
Public validate/check accepted and outcome fields agree in every retained run; UI transition results are retained independently.

definitions.conclusiveGradeAgreement: Expected true requires accepted=true/outcome=correct; expected false requires accepted=false/outcome=incorrect. Unknown and incomplete never count.
definitions.caseSequence: Observe literal x/X/y/Y in order per line, skipping TeX control words and control symbols. Preserve case and line boundaries; no variable equivalence or text repair.
definitions.exact: Copied source compareOcrTex metrics; explicit TeX row separators preserve line boundaries. Normalization is syntactic, not mathematical equivalence.
definitions.operationWhitespaceOnlyAgreement: Compare source expectedOperations/actualOperations after deleting whitespace from each non-null string; preserve nulls/order. Source operationTextExact flags remain unchanged.
definitions.measuredAt: Source report measurement timestamp, not asserted completion time.

parts.source: Authored normalized glyphs and layouts. No pupil records, screenshots, telemetry or captured handwriting.
parts.splitPolicy: All variants of one baseTaskId share a fixed split. Holdout means excluded from development tuning; reporting a holdout result consumes that evaluation.
parts.limitation: This small synthetic development/holdout sample measures specific pipeline behavior, not general handwriting accuracy. Deliberately wrong calculations have deliberately wrong transcription targets.

parts.source: Authored vector letter styles plus existing authored mathematical glyphs; no pupil data, screenshots, recorded handwriting or repository PNG files.
parts.splitPolicy: All numerical task variants and variable renamings share a baseTaskId and split. Both intentionally ambiguous twins are development controls, never holdout examples.
parts.limitation: This fixed synthetic probe measures case-sensitive transcription and grading behavior, not general handwriting accuracy. Clear examples and ambiguous controls must be reported separately; the latter have conflicting authored targets for identical pixels.

corpus.limitation: Combined authored development and previously evaluated task holdout. Pixel-identical ambiguous letter controls are reported separately and cannot establish a unique intended case.

observations.divisionNote: :3 changes linear-valid from unknown to correct and reduces calls eight to five. :5 changes holdout-linear from incorrect to correct with five calls. Deliberately wrong 15 and final 4 remain written and rejected. Single-run observations, not general latency estimates.

dpr2Diagnostic.observation: All three division probes retain :3/:5. Old cross-style final variables are read as X instead of x, making linear-valid and holdout-linear incorrect. Both mixed x/X probes retain the same wrong initial variable sequences as DPR1. No evidence for improved recognition from higher pixel density or a preprocessing default change.

cases.intentionalError: The authored wrong 15 and final 4 must be transcribed unchanged. Correcting either number is an OCR error.

cases.measurementGap: Joint OCR of superscript, subscript, plus-minus and root is measured without assuming it succeeds.
Roman labels and separate system rows are an OCR coverage probe, not prevalidated handwriting recognition.
Completion with indexed branches measures composition of multiple OCR structures.
The authored word Probe and its separate numeric check are an OCR coverage probe.

cases.intentionalError: The written middle row changes x to X. Correct final assignments do not justify this false step; OCR must retain the uppercase X.
The written middle row changes y to Y. The uppercase Y must stay in the transcription despite the correct final assignments.

cases.measurementGap: The target records author intent only. This case is not evidence that an ambiguous cross can be uniquely recognized.

ambiguity.explanation: The lowercase-intent and uppercase-intent twins have identical strokes and the same task prompt. Their exact authored targets differ. Pixels alone do not identify the intended case; report ambiguity and never equate x with X or repair the written answer using the task solution.

cases.intentionalError: The author intended X throughout an answer to a task about x. The identical cross raster cannot establish that intent. Do not silently substitute x to obtain an accepted answer.
cases.measurementGap: An observationally identical pair with incompatible exact targets must be reported as an ambiguity control, not an attainable joint exactness target.
